findings.evidence: plot.py draws head at zorder 3 with markersize 5 (lines 60-71) and then, for base, an additional white-faced square scatter at s=45, zorder 4 (lines 72-82), which paints over the head line and marker. Measured on image-0.png in the booking panel's plateau (render rows 144-165, columns 1088-1114): blue ink fills rows 148-151 up to the square's left edge, is absent across the square's white interior, and resumes at the same rows on its right edge.
findings.summary: The base series' marker is drawn above the head series with a white face, so wherever the two arms coincide the head line and its marker are erased and the reader sees an open grey square with a broken blue line. The subject series is the one the figure reports on, yet it is the one that disappears exactly where the arms agree, which is the figure's headline. It stays non-blocking because the blue line enters and leaves each square at the same height, so the head value at every occluded iterate is still readable, and the interruption itself shows where base sits on head. A reader who did not know the two arms overlap could, however, mistake the missing head ink for missing data at those iterates.

rubric_lines: RUBRIC legibility: pass. Four log-y panels in a 2x2 grid, one per residual block ('full relative error', 'booking relative error', 'geometry relative error', 'flux relative error'), x axis 'accepted iterate' labelled 0-9 on the bottom row only, one frameless two-entry legend above the panels. A reader can name each panel's quantity, read each decade and follow both arms across all ten iterates. The one reading cost is the head marker being erased under the base marker where the two coincide, recorded as finding 1; the head level at those points is still readable from the line entering and leaving the marker at the same height.

RUBRIC data_ink: pass. Two line-and-marker series per panel and nothing else inside the axes, apart from the log scale that makes the values readable. Measured on the render: 6599 px of the head blue #2865b2 and 2482 px of the base grey #929292 across the whole canvas, and no shaded region, band or area fill anywhere.

RUBRIC decoration: pass. Top and right spines are absent, no gridline is drawn, no background fill or drop shadow, and the y tick ladder is thinned to at most about four labelled decades per panel (for example 1e-11 and 1e-10 in the flux panel) rather than a full set.

RUBRIC contrast: pass. Head blue #2865b2 is about 5.9:1 on white; base grey #929292 is about 3.1:1, at the 3:1 graphics floor and separated from the head arm by its white-faced square marker as well as its hue; all axis, tick and legend text is near-black on white.

RUBRIC table_form: pass. Ten accepted iterates against four error blocks, two arms overlaid per panel, is a trend comparison; the fragment carries the numeric ladder as a table and this image carries what the table cannot show at a glance, namely that the two arms lie on one another.

RUBRIC label_collision: pass. No label is clipped or overlaps another label or the data: the render's ink bounding box is rows 3-685 and columns 137-1372 of a 720x1399 canvas, with zero non-white pixels in the left, right and bottom 4-px frames and 40 px in the top frame, all of them the tops of the legend text at rows 3-7, so nothing is cut. The drawing script refuses to save when any text artist is clipped or two overlap (plot.py check_text), and the render agrees with that check.
